label: Era Language
description: Buildings speaking one era's design language fluently.

items.name: romanesque-priory
items.text: a Romanesque priory, round arches on squat drum columns, fortress-thick walls letting in arrow-slit light

items.name: palladian-villa
items.text: a Palladian villa in honey stone, temple portico and shallow dome in perfect bilateral symmetry above terraced lawns

items.name: victorian-gothic
items.text: a High Victorian Gothic hall, polychrome brick banding, pointed arcades, iron roof cresting bristling with finials

items.name: streamline-moderne
items.text: a streamline-moderne seaside pavilion, rounded white decks stacked like an ocean liner, porthole windows and tubular chrome rails

items.name: bauhaus-block
items.text: a Bauhaus workshop block, crisp white render, ribbon windows, a glass curtain corner turned without a single column

items.name: googie-diner
items.text: a googie roadside diner, upswept butterfly roof on splayed steel legs, starburst sign and acres of plate glass

items.name: metabolist-capsules
items.text: a metabolist tower of bolted-on living capsules, round portholes stacked in a concrete crate, seams and service cores left exposed

items.name: deconstructivist-museum
items.text: a deconstructivist museum, torqued titanium sheets colliding at impossible angles, reflections sliding off every non-parallel wall

items.name: beaux-arts-station
items.text: a Beaux-Arts railway terminal, coffered barrel vault on paired Corinthian columns, clerestory lunettes laying wide bands of light across the marble concourse

items.name: georgian-terrace
items.text: a Georgian terrace in soot-warmed brick, sash windows diminishing floor by floor in strict proportion, fanlights over paneled doors, wrought-iron railings guarding the basement areas

items.name: high-tech-exoskeleton
items.text: a high-tech building worn inside-out, structural exoskeleton and color-coded service ducts hung on the facade, glass lifts climbing the frame in plain view

items.name: prairie-house
items.text: a Prairie-style house hugging its ground line, deep cantilevered eaves stretched horizontal, ribbon casement windows under low hipped roofs, brick joints raked to stress the long courses
